findings.title: Agent said goodbye at 4:10.7 while the call was still going
findings.summary: The agent ended its side of the conversation although the other side had not wrapped up; the conversation continued afterwards.

evidence.label: User's previous turn (no closing)
evidence.value: Okay, let's go with Thursday at 8 AM, 2 weeks from now.

evidence.label: Agent said goodbye
evidence.value: Okay, that works. Thank you for your help. Goodbye.

evidence.label: Conversation continued
evidence.value: One moment, please. I'm checking your information.

evidence.label: Agent instruction about goodbyes
evidence.value: Once your appointment is confirmed, thank them and say goodbye.

root_cause.statement: The agent treated agreement on a detail as the end of the call; its instructions tie goodbye to that moment.
missing_evidence: A re-run of the same script with the goodbye instruction rewritten

next_steps: Instruct the agent to say goodbye only after the other side wraps up.
Re-run the same script and check that the goodbye moves to the end.

findings.title: Agent held its reply for 2.21s before speaking
findings.summary: At 0:21.1 the agent held its prepared reply because of user voice activity that never produced a transcript, adding 2.21s before it spoke.

evidence.label: Agent reply affected
evidence.value: Hi Sarah. I need to schedule a follow-up appointment with Dr. Patel. My lower back pain has come back over the last two weeks.

root_cause.statement: A short sound on the user's side (breath, filler, noise) was treated as a possible interruption.
missing_evidence: Microphone audio at the trigger time

next_steps: Listen to the microphone channel at the trigger time.
Re-run the same script with headphones and compare false-interruption counts.
Lower false_interruption_timeout (default 2.0s) to shorten the gap, or raise min_interruption_duration if short sounds are the trigger.

findings.title: 2 of 30 user turns ended by the 2.5s endpointing timeout
findings.summary: For these turns the turn detector never judged the user finished, so the agent waited the full 2.5s before replying.

evidence.label: End-of-turn delay at 0:52.0
evidence.value: 2.501s: 'Could you please spell your first and last name for me?'

evidence.label: Agent response latency after these turns

root_cause.statement: The user paused or trailed off mid-thought, so end-of-turn prediction stayed uncertain until the maximum delay.

next_steps: Read the timed-out turns: are they fragments or complete sentences?
If complete, check turn-detector settings; if fragments, the wait was correct.
Avoid lowering max_endpointing_delay blindly: it would cut users off mid-sentence.
